### **Job Description and Duties**


As a matrixed multi\-disciplinary environmental team, the Environmental Services Branch provides comprehensive and specialized environmental regulatory compliance services to support the Department's wide range of activities. Under the general direction of the Manager in the CEQA and NEPA Support Section, the incumbent supervises and directs the work activities of the Hazardous Materials and Environmental Evaluations Unit (HAZMATEE). HAZMATEE provides comprehensive environmental site assessment, document preparation, permitting, surveying, monitoring, environmental sampling and analysis, and consultant oversight services to ensure DWR's compliance with applicable federal, State, and local environmental laws and regulations in support of DWR's continued operation and maintenance of the State Water Project; flood risk reduction activities; and restoration of the State's ecosystem. This position works collaboratively and in close coordination with the Environmental Assessments and Permitting Section, which ensures multi\-disciplinary support amongst the Branch, Division, and Department\-wide, and with federal, State, and local agencies and interested parties.  

  

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

Department of Water Resources (DWR) was established in 1956 by the California State Legislature. We manage California’s water resources, systems, and infrastructure, including the State Water Project, in a responsible sustainable way.


At DWR, we are embedding climate change response into every project we undertake. We have set standards to help evaluate how each project incorporates climate resilience principles and ensure consistency across the Department. Our mission is to sustainably manage the water resources of California, in cooperation with other agencies, to benefit the state’s people and protect, restore, and enhance the natural and human environments.


DWR also strives to create a trusting and welcoming workplace where employees embrace diverse viewpoints and treat each other with civility and respect. An important component of DWR’s equal employment opportunity program centers around justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion.


Department Website: https://water.ca.gov/


Free virtual career consultation services including one\-on\-one DWR career consultations, application/resume review, tips for applying, and mock interviews, provided by DWR’s Recruitment and Workforce Planning section can now be scheduled via https://water.ca.gov/About/Careers.  

### **Special Requirements**


Incumbent must have experience working with applicable federal, State, and local environmental regulatory agencies, such as U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, California Environmental Protection Agency (Cal/EPA), California Department of Fish and Game, and Certified Unified Program Agencies (CUPAs).  

Incumbent must have knowledge of multi\-media sampling procedures, techniques, and equipment; sample preparation and handling; analytical laboratory methods; and quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) measures. Incumbent must be willing to work extended hours on occasion.
  

  

Incumbent must possess a valid California State driver's license in order to drive to various environmental site assessment locations.  

Incumbent must also be able to lift at least 25 pounds, pass a baseline medical examination, be physically capable of using an air purifying respirator or self\-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA), and complete a 40\-hour Hazardous Waste Operations \& Emergency Response (HAZWOPER) course and an 8\-hour refresher course, annually thereafter, pursuant to OSHA Standard 29CFR 1910\.120 and Title 8, CCR 5192\.

### **Job Description and Duties**


Do you want to support the ecological and economic well\-being of one of the largest estuaries on the West Coast? The Sacramento\-San Joaquin Delta Conservancy (Conservancy) is seeking an Environmental Scientist to initiate, manage, and close out projects, including those for the Conservancy's Ecosystem Restoration and Climate Adaptation Program. This position provides an exciting opportunity to advance projects related to nature\-based solutions, climate resiliency, ecosystem restoration, and agricultural sustainability in the Sacramento\-San Joaquin Delta (Delta) and Suisun Marsh. The Conservancy is a small, committed team that works across departments and disciplines to protect, enhance, and restore the Delta's economy, agriculture and working landscapes, and environment.
  

  

In this position you will:


* Manage, monitor, and close\-out projects by monitoring performance and status by tracking deliverables, budgets, and expenditures.
* Prepare and review agreements, reports, memos, documents, and invoices for the Ecosystem Restoration and Climate Adaptation Program.
* Participate in community outreach and educate interested parties about the Conservancy, its programs, and issues of importance in the Delta and Suisun Marsh
* Communicate with diverse collection of interested parties (e.g., environmental non\-profits, regional conversation districts, public agencies) by preparing and presenting scientific reports, factsheets, workshops, and trainings.
* Identify, research, and address issues related to nature\-based solutions, climate resiliency, ecosystem restoration, and agricultural sustainability and apply for funding for projects to implement them.
* Aid Conservancy staff and management with program implementation and special projects related to environmental concerns in the Delta and Suisun Marsh.

  

Come join a team that creates:
  

* A team atmosphere founded upon ethics, integrity, and stewardship.
* A positive work environment that is open to change and invites its workforce to challenge processes.
* An opportunity for individuals to utilize their knowledge, skills, and experience to grow within the department.
  

  

This position is Limited Term (12 months); it may become permanent, be extended up to 24 months, or be cancelled at any time.
  

  

**This position is designated under the Conflict of Interest Code.** The position is responsible for making or participating in the making of governmental decisions that may potentially have a material effect on personal financial interests. The appointee is required to complete Form 700 within 30 days of appointment and once per year.
  

  

This position may require travel.
  

  

**This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship by the start date of employment. * Ability to plan, organize, communicate, adapt to changing assignments and priorities, and work effectively under pressure to meet deadlines
* Experience drafting RFPs, RFQs, IFB, and related Minimum Qualifications (MQs)
* Experience using Microsoft Office Suite, MS Teams, Visio, SharePoint, and data visualization tools such as PowerBI, GIS and Tableau
* Experience gathering, identifying, analyzing, reading, and interpreting data from surveys and evaluation
* Experience leading and facilitating large meetings using verbal and written communication skills to present information to all levels of stakeholders, management, administrative and programmatic staff, and solution partners

Are you looking for an exciting and fulfilling career in geology/hydrogeology and agricultural engineering? If you enjoy a career helping others and working in an office and field environment, then this may be the position for you! Apply today and join our team. The Central Valley Regional Water Quality Control Board has an opening for an Engineering Geologist (EG) in the Confined Animals Unit. The position is located at 11020 Sun Center Drive, Rancho Cordova, CA 95670, right off Highway 50, which is within a pleasant business park with walking paths, nearby restaurants, and shops.


Duties: Priority specific EG duties include the following:


* Perform technical assessments of engineering reports and review and evaluate water quality data from technical and monitoring reports for assigned facilities.
* Using engineering geologic judgment and technical data from observations, self\-monitoring reports, and sampling, ascertain dischargers' compliance with basin plan, waste discharge requirements (WDRs), Regional and State Water Board policies and regulations.
* Review groundwater monitoring work plans and monitoring results of assigned cases to determine compliance with WDRs.
* Evaluate environmental and engineering data relating to the design and performance of assigned facilities.
* Evaluate sampling points and laboratory techniques.
* Perform engineering and geotechnical reviews on matters relating to liner and cover construction, soil characteristics, waste constituent loading, groundwater hydrogeology, and receiving water assimilative capacities of assigned cases.
* Using engineering geologic judgment, prepare all necessary documentation such as letters, memorandums, reports, and enforcement orders resulting from evaluation of an assigned technical report.

CDFW North Central Region (Region 2\) Habitat Conservation Program is hiring! From high mountain meadows to Sacramento Valley floodplains, we're looking for a passionate scientist ready to invest in a resilient restoration future that meets the needs of California's ecosystems.

Confluence Environmental is a well\-established environmental services company, providing environmental services to various large\-scale engineering, consulting, and energy firms. We are looking for enthusiastic and eager candidates for an entry level position as an Environmental Technician to join our growing team in our Northern California (greater Sacramento).

Environmental Field Technicians work independently, driving company provided trucks to various job sites collecting groundwater samples. The technicians operate various large equipment including generators, air compressors, pumps, and pressure washers to assist in groundwater removal and monitoring wells. ### **Job Description and Duties**


**Why Join DHCS?**  

  

The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) is the backbone of California’s health care safety net. Our success is made possible by the hard work of more than 4,800 DHCS team members and through collaboration with the federal government and other state agencies, counties, and partners for the care of low\-income families, children, pregnant women, older adults, and persons with disabilities. This is an exciting opportunity to join our diverse team in the following role. If you are interested in joining our team, apply today!  



  

**About this Role:**


Under general direction of the Manager II in the Managed Care Mointoring Branch, the Research Data Specialist III (RDS III) serves as a senior research and data expert supporting compliance monitoring required under the Managed Care Final Rule and the broader oversight of the Medi\-Cal Managed Care program. The role leads advanced research, analytical, and monitoring activities that inform program enforcement within the managed care delivery system. Positioned within a program division rather than a traditional data unit, the incumbent focuses on coordination, collaboration, and liaison work with the Department’s data and technology partners including the Program Data Reporting Division (PDRD), Health Information Management Division (HIMD), and Enterprise Technology Services (ETS). In partnership with these divisions, the RDS III contributes to the development and refinement of monitoring methodologies, shared data exchange processes, and databases and reporting tools used to track grievances, appeals, audit findings, and corrective action plan outcomes tied to Final Rule requirements. Key responsibilities include translating program needs into clear business requirements, participating in the joint development and validation of monitoring datasets, and interpreting results to support oversight and enforcement. The RDS III identifies anomalies, emerging trends, and potential indicators of non\-compliance, elevating issues to program leadership when necessary. The position also provides leadership, consultation, and training to staff and collaborates closely with Medi\-Cal managed care plans (MCPs), other governmental agencies, and internal partners to ensure accurate, consistent, and meaningful reporting. The RDS III documents methodologies and findings and produces high\-quality reports, dashboards, and presentations that communicate monitoring results and support program decision\-making.

This position is a special and unique opportunity to work in some of the most beautiful watersheds in the state of California, studying and enhancing salmon and steelhead populations primarily in the Eel River and watersheds of the Mendocino Coast. Work is related to state and federal Endangered Species Act listed stocks and management of valued fisheries for the state and tribes on the North Coast. Promoting collaboration with partners in order to leverage collective resources is encouraged. This position stands to make a positive and real difference for trust resources and those that value them. Under the general guidance of the Coastal Fisheries Environmental Program Manager, the incumbent supervises the Coastal Watershed Planning and Assessment Program. The Program includes a broad suite of monitoring, assessment, restoration, and regulatory activities in Humboldt and Mendocino Counties. These activities include monitoring and assessment of fish life history, fish distribution, recovery, permitting, ecosystem assessment, restoration planning, and annual sportfish regulations. This position will oversee or support various aquatic resource plans, restoration and monitoring plans, and several monitoring and assessment activities related specifically to the Eel River and potential dam removal. The incumbent manages a complex budget, helps develop and manage large scale ecosystem assessments, and develops and manages complex contracts or grants with ecological scope. As such the position entails significant grant/contract writing and management responsibilities. This includes planning, directing, and coordinating all aspects of development and implementation of detailed and watershed\-specific monitoring and research programs for salmon, steelhead, and other trout populations. Responsibilities are varied and include analyzing complex environmental issues, requiring a high level of personal initiative in the application of sound scientific methods and ecological principles to natural resource assessment, management, planning and habitat restoration activities. Incumbent will represent the Department in dealings with local, State and federal governmental agencies, Tribal partners, conservation groups and private landowners. Area of geographic responsibility includes all nine Northern California counties that make up the Northern Region, however duties will be largely focused in Humboldt and Mendocino Counties. Performance of specified duties requires a comprehensive knowledge of administrative procedures, Department policies, applicable environmental law, and complex ecological principals. ### **Job Description and Duties**


The California Coastal Commission is seeking an experienced Environmental Scientist or Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to join its Ecology Team (Technical Services Unit) at its Headquarters Office in downtown San Francisco. This position will primarily focus on the relationship between wildfire and coastal ecology as relates to vegetation management for fuel reduction, ecological restoration, and resilience work across a range of ecosystems, including forests, shrublands, grasslands and wetlands throughout the coastal zone, which extends inland from the shoreline at variable distances up to more than five miles in some areas.


The Commission is a small State agency that is charged with protecting coastal resources and managing coastal development in California. The Commission’s mission is to implement the Coastal Act and to protect, restore, and enhance coastal and marine resources for the continuing benefit of current and future generations. It carries out this mandate through regulatory and planning actions related to development within offshore waters and on land along the California coast. The Commission also has authority under the federal Coastal Zone Management Act to review federal and federally\-permitted activities such as dredging, military training exercises, wildland management, and highway projects that affect resources of the coastal zone.


The Ecology Team generally supports the Commission and its staff with technical review and analysis of potential effects on the coast’s sensitive natural resources associated with proposed development projects. Under the direction of the Ecology Team Manager, the successful incumbent will be integrated into the existing team of five ecologists and work with Commission staff to address ecological issues raised in the Commission’s policy, planning, and regulatory work as relates to wildfire resilience and risk reduction efforts. This work will focus on understanding and addressing the ecological effects of vegetation management for fuel reduction and wildfire resilience, including through ecological restoration, throughout the coastal zone. It will necessitate cooperation with other scientific and technical teams such as Mapping and Water Quality, coordination with the Commission’s Statewide Planning Unit, and provision of scientific support to staff and the Commission. Duties will be adjusted commensurately to the level at which the position is filled. Generally, the incumbent will be expected to: review and analyze a variety of technical reports including CEQA/NEPA documents, technical surveys and memoranda, restoration and mitigation plans, and scientific literature; conduct research and investigations often involving complex environmental conditions and circumstances; identify problems including potential adverse impacts to coastal resources and means to avoid and minimize these; factor in climate change dynamics relative to environmental considerations; coordinate with other federal, state, and local agencies; and, make recommendations for conformance with the natural resource policies of the Coastal Act and relevant certified plans.


Key functions of the job include: analyzing proposed fire resilience and risk reduction work for consistency with applicable Coastal Act policies; tracking topical scientific literature including white papers and peer\-reviewed publications; guiding related policy based on scientific understanding of the issues and existing frameworks; developing recommendations on how to avoid and minimize adverse impacts to native habitat (including for communities and species) associated with fuel reduction and vegetation management efforts across the landscape while advancing ecological resilience; contributing to the development of recommendations for Commission regulatory action, including staff reports, permit conditions, and planning documents; communicating with project proponents; updating and maintaining a spatial database of authorized fire resilience and risk reduction work and conducting geospatial analyses; reviewing monitoring and mitigation plans and reports; participating in site visits and inspections to evaluate on\-the\-ground ecological conditions; writing technical memoranda to support and accompany staff reports and recommendations; and providing technical presentations at public meetings. The incumbent may also represent the Commission staff on multi\-agency work groups, task forces, and similar entities; and coordinate with staff of local, state, and federal agencies; the legislature; stakeholder groups; and the broader public.


The position offers considerable opportunity for developing and contributing expertise on a range of ecosystems as well as relevant and emerging issues related to coastal ecology and wildfire resilience in California’s coastal landscape.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

The California Coastal Commission’s Headquarters is located in downtown San Francisco. The employee will work Monday through Friday. Telework is available for this position in accordance with the California Coastal Commission’s Telework Policy and Proc

The Occupational Health Branch (OHB) is part of the Center for Healthy Communities (CHC). **Job Description**

**Please note:** **All applications must be submitted no later than 11:59pm PT on September 10\.**

**The University of Washington School of Medicine Academic, Rural, and Regional Affairs team has an outstanding opportunity for a FCM Program Coordinator to join their team.**

**About this Opportunity**

Reporting to the Foundations of Clinical Medicine (FCM) Operations Specialist, the FCM Program Coordinator is responsible for delivering exceptional operational, curriculum, and program support for the UW School of Medicine Spokane Medical Education Office at Gonzaga University. This highly collaborative role partners with faculty, students, physicians, and administrative teams to help create a seamless educational experience across Foundations of Clinical Medicine, Primary Care Practicum, the Colleges program, and clinical learning experiences. This position is located in Spokane, Washington and offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to the training of future physicians.


**Key Responsibilities**

**Medical Student Curriculum Support (60%)**

* Serve as the primary point of contact for student\-facing support, communication, onboarding activities, and clinical compliance tracking.
* Coordinate and execute logistics for clinical skills workshops, exams, hospital tutorials, student schedules, and Canvas course sites.
* Lead administration of the Standardized Patient program, including recruitment, scheduling, documentation, orientation support, and supply coordination.
* Facilitate student clinical experiences by managing scheduling updates, hospital badge processes, credentialing coordination, and activity tracking.
* Support faculty mentors and educational events through event planning, vendor coordination, reimbursement processing, and program logistics.

**Office Administration (30%)**

* Develop and maintain reports, correspondence, presentations, calendars, databases, and other administrative resources supporting educational programs.
* Maintain student and community preceptor records while ensuring data accuracy through research, fact\-checking, and ongoing updates.
* Provide classroom technology support and troubleshoot instructional materials for workshops, examinations, and learning sessions.
* Support budget reconciliation, office purchasing, inventory management, and receipt processing through Workday.

**Special Projects and Event Planning (10%)**

* Coordinate special projects, events, and cross\-functional initiatives that enhance the student and faculty experience.
* Reserve and manage instructional and event spaces while supporting event logistics and project implementation.
* Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned in support of program and department goals.

**Required Qualifications**

To be considered for this opportunity your application must demonstrate you meet both the minimum qualifications and additional qualifications listed below. Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.


**Minimum Qualifications**

* High school graduation or equivalent AND two years of experience in an academic setting with a high\-volume of processes.
* Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.

Applicants who do not meet these qualifications WILL NOT be forwarded to the Hiring Manager.


**Additional Qualifications**

* Advanced word processing skills with an emphasis on Microsoft Office products to include MS Word, Excel, Access, Outlook, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and OneDrive.
* Expertise with internet search and research, fact checking, and cross reference skills.
* Strong interpersonal skills to interact effectively with community, employees, management, students, and physicians.
* Excellent organizing and prioritizing skills with the ability to multitask and work under the pressure of constant deadlines.
* Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy in all forms of communication.
* Ability to work independently while being in a high functioning team.
* Discretion with senior\-level confidential student information.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Associate or Bachelor’s degree.
* Two years of progressively independent and complex administrative support experience.
* Work experience in a health care setting or directly with physicians, and/or in higher education is strongly preferred.
* Advanced experience with Excel, Sharepoint, and Asana programs.

**Working Conditions**

* Occasional work beyond a standard 40\-hour work week may be required.
* Periodic evening and weekend work may be necessary to support events, presentations, meetings, and project deadlines.
* This position is overtime eligible.

The UW School of Medicine Spokane Medical Education Office is committed to delivering an exceptional medical education experience that prepares future physicians to serve diverse communities. CDFW North Central Region (Region 2\) Habitat Conservation Program is hiring! From high mountain meadows to Sacramento Valley floodplains, we're looking for a passionate scientist ready to invest in a resilient restoration future that meets the needs of California's ecosystems.


Under the general direction of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) in the Habitat Conservation Program within the North Central Region Water Resources and Infrastructure unit, this position serves in a lead role as part of a statewide team that assists in the administration of the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) Cutting the Green Tape (CGT) Program, to increase the pace, scale, and quality of environmental restoration through coordination of restoration project development, expedited environmental review and permitting pathways, and restoration grant management.

**Position: Environmental Field Technician**  
**Location: Rio Linda**

**About Us**  
Confluence Environmental is a well\-established environmental services company, providing environmental services to various large\-scale engineering, consulting, and energy firms. We are looking for enthusiastic and eager candidates for an entry level position as an Environmental Technician to join our growing team in our Northern California (greater Sacramento).

**Job Description**  
Environmental Field Technicians work independently, driving company provided trucks to various job sites collecting groundwater samples. The technicians operate various large equipment including generators, air compressors, pumps, and pressure washers to assist in groundwater removal and monitoring wells. Our technician’s test for water parameters using field meters, take precise notes and collect water samples that will be processed in a laboratory for analysis. We offer on the job training and are willing to work with motivated individuals.

* Must have outdoor work experience and be willing and able to work outdoors 100% of the time in all weather conditions.
* Must be mechanically inclined with experience operating and troubleshooting tools and equipment.

* Valid California Driver’s License with a clean DMV record
* Ability to read maps.
* Comfortable driving Ford 450 Super Duty trucks or Large Sprinter Vans and occasionally pulling a trailer.
* Must be available to travel overnight 50% of the time.
* Must have the ability to work full time.

**Why Join DHCS?**  

  

The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) is the backbone of California’s health care safety net. Our success is made possible by the hard work of more than 4,800 DHCS team members and through collaboration with the federal government and other state agencies, counties, and partners for the care of low\-income families, children, pregnant women, older adults, and persons with disabilities. This is an exciting opportunity to join our diverse team in the following role. If you are interested in joining our team, apply today!  



  

**About this Role:**


Under general direction of the Manager II in the Managed Care Mointoring Branch, the Research Data Specialist III (RDS III) serves as a senior research and data expert supporting compliance monitoring required under the Managed Care Final Rule and the broader oversight of the Medi\-Cal Managed Care program. The role leads advanced research, analytical, and monitoring activities that inform program enforcement within the managed care delivery system. Positioned within a program division rather than a traditional data unit, the incumbent focuses on coordination, collaboration, and liaison work with the Department’s data and technology partners including the Program Data Reporting Division (PDRD), Health Information Management Division (HIMD), and Enterprise Technology Services (ETS). In partnership with these divisions, the RDS III contributes to the development and refinement of monitoring methodologies, shared data exchange processes, and databases and reporting tools used to track grievances, appeals, audit findings, and corrective action plan outcomes tied to Final Rule requirements. Key responsibilities include translating program needs into clear business requirements, participating in the joint development and validation of monitoring datasets, and interpreting results to support oversight and enforcement. The RDS III identifies anomalies, emerging trends, and potential indicators of non\-compliance, elevating issues to program leadership when necessary. The position also provides leadership, consultation, and training to staff and collaborates closely with Medi\-Cal managed care plans (MCPs), other governmental agencies, and internal partners to ensure accurate, consistent, and meaningful reporting. The RDS III documents methodologies and findings and produces high\-quality reports, dashboards, and presentations that communicate monitoring results and support program decision\-making.

This position is a special and unique opportunity to work in some of the most beautiful watersheds in the state of California, studying and enhancing salmon and steelhead populations primarily in the Eel River and watersheds of the Mendocino Coast. Work is related to state and federal Endangered Species Act listed stocks and management of valued fisheries for the state and tribes on the North Coast. Promoting collaboration with partners in order to leverage collective resources is encouraged. This position stands to make a positive and real difference for trust resources and those that value them. Under the general guidance of the Coastal Fisheries Environmental Program Manager, the incumbent supervises the Coastal Watershed Planning and Assessment Program. The Program includes a broad suite of monitoring, assessment, restoration, and regulatory activities in Humboldt and Mendocino Counties. These activities include monitoring and assessment of fish life history, fish distribution, recovery, permitting, ecosystem assessment, restoration planning, and annual sportfish regulations. This position will oversee or support various aquatic resource plans, restoration and monitoring plans, and several monitoring and assessment activities related specifically to the Eel River and potential dam removal. The incumbent manages a complex budget, helps develop and manage large scale ecosystem assessments, and develops and manages complex contracts or grants with ecological scope. As such the position entails significant grant/contract writing and management responsibilities. This includes planning, directing, and coordinating all aspects of development and implementation of detailed and watershed\-specific monitoring and research programs for salmon, steelhead, and other trout populations. Responsibilities are varied and include analyzing complex environmental issues, requiring a high level of personal initiative in the application of sound scientific methods and ecological principles to natural resource assessment, management, planning and habitat restoration activities. Incumbent will represent the Department in dealings with local, State and federal governmental agencies, Tribal partners, conservation groups and private landowners. Area of geographic responsibility includes all nine Northern California counties that make up the Northern Region, however duties will be largely focused in Humboldt and Mendocino Counties. Performance of specified duties requires a comprehensive knowledge of administrative procedures, Department policies, applicable environmental law, and complex ecological principals. **Site Supervision \& Environmental Compliance**


* Undertake regular environmental inspections of construction and work areas.
* Identify, record and report environmental issues, providing advice on appropriate remedial actions.
* Provide practical environmental guidance to contractors and project teams on site.

**Ecological Surveys \& Monitoring**


* Provide on\-site ecological advice and support during construction activities.
* Undertake ecological walkover surveys, assessments and species\-specific checks.
* Support the supervision of works taking place within or near sensitive habitats.

**Environmental Reporting \& Documentation**


* Provide written and verbal advice on environmental legislation, permits, consents and environmental planning constraints.
* Prepare daily site records, compliance reports and ecological monitoring documentation.
* Maintain accurate records of environmental observations and actions.

**Environmental Performance**


* Gather, monitor and collate environmental performance information across project activities.
* Support the implementation of initiatives designed to improve environmental performance and minimise environmental impacts.

**Compliance \& Environmental Management**


* Support compliance with relevant environmental legislation and project requirements.
* Review and update Environmental Management Plans to ensure they remain compliant with legislation, consents and best practice.
* Support internal audits and self\-assessments of site activities against applicable legislation, processes, procedures and environmental standards.
* Assist in demonstrating compliance with environmental protection measures and equipment requirements.

**Project Support \& Stakeholder Engagement**


* Support the planning and coordination of environmental deliverables across projects.
* Work closely with senior environmental and ecological specialists to achieve project objectives.
* Liaise with contractors, clients and other stakeholders to ensure environmental requirements are understood and effectively implemented.
* Act as an on\-site point of contact for environmental and ecological matters.
  
**My profile**
--------------


We are looking for an experienced environmental professional with a strong combination of **environmental management and construction\-site experience**.


You will ideally have:


* Experience working in an environmental management role, with practical on\-site environmental and ecological experience.
* Detailed knowledge of UK environmental legislation relevant to construction or industrial installations, alongside relevant guidance, industry standards and best practice.
* Experience undertaking environmental or ecological fieldwork and supervising works in sensitive habitats.
* Experience working within an Environmental Management System (EMS) aligned with **BS EN ISO 14001:2015**.
* The confidence to work independently and influence contractors, project teams and stakeholders.
* Excellent communication, interpersonal and influencing skills.
* Strong organisational and time\-management skills, with the ability to prioritise effectively within a complex and fast\-moving project environment.
* An understanding of the client/contractor relationship and legal responsibilities under the **Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2007 (CDM)** would be desirable.
* A degree or equivalent qualification in an environmental, engineering or science\-related discipline.
* A full UK or EU driving licence and willingness to travel to active construction and remote project sites across Lancashire and the wider region.
* A valid **CSCS Card**.
* Chartered status or membership of a relevant professional environmental body, such as **ISEP**, would be desirable.
  
What We Offer

**Job Description**

**Please note:** **All applications must be submitted no later than 11:59pm PT on September 10\.**

**The University of Washington School of Medicine Academic, Rural, and Regional Affairs team has an outstanding opportunity for a FCM Program Coordinator to join their team.**

**About this Opportunity**

Reporting to the Foundations of Clinical Medicine (FCM) Operations Specialist, the FCM Program Coordinator is responsible for delivering exceptional operational, curriculum, and program support for the UW School of Medicine Spokane Medical Education Office at Gonzaga University. This highly collaborative role partners with faculty, students, physicians, and administrative teams to help create a seamless educational experience across Foundations of Clinical Medicine, Primary Care Practicum, the Colleges program, and clinical learning experiences. This position is located in Spokane, Washington and offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to the training of future physicians.


**Key Responsibilities**

**Medical Student Curriculum Support (60%)**

* Serve as the primary point of contact for student\-facing support, communication, onboarding activities, and clinical compliance tracking.
* Coordinate and execute logistics for clinical skills workshops, exams, hospital tutorials, student schedules, and Canvas course sites.
* Lead administration of the Standardized Patient program, including recruitment, scheduling, documentation, orientation support, and supply coordination.
* Facilitate student clinical experiences by managing scheduling updates, hospital badge processes, credentialing coordination, and activity tracking.
* Support faculty mentors and educational events through event planning, vendor coordination, reimbursement processing, and program logistics.

**Office Administration (30%)**

* Develop and maintain reports, correspondence, presentations, calendars, databases, and other administrative resources supporting educational programs.
* Maintain student and community preceptor records while ensuring data accuracy through research, fact\-checking, and ongoing updates.
* Provide classroom technology support and troubleshoot instructional materials for workshops, examinations, and learning sessions.
* Support budget reconciliation, office purchasing, inventory management, and receipt processing through Workday.

**Special Projects and Event Planning (10%)**

* Coordinate special projects, events, and cross\-functional initiatives that enhance the student and faculty experience.
* Reserve and manage instructional and event spaces while supporting event logistics and project implementation.
* Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned in support of program and department goals.

**Required Qualifications**

To be considered for this opportunity your application must demonstrate you meet both the minimum qualifications and additional qualifications listed below. Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.


**Minimum Qualifications**

* High school graduation or equivalent AND two years of experience in an academic setting with a high\-volume of processes.
* Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.

Applicants who do not meet these qualifications WILL NOT be forwarded to the Hiring Manager.


**Additional Qualifications**

* Advanced word processing skills with an emphasis on Microsoft Office products to include MS Word, Excel, Access, Outlook, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and OneDrive.
* Expertise with internet search and research, fact checking, and cross reference skills.
* Strong interpersonal skills to interact effectively with community, employees, management, students, and physicians.
* Excellent organizing and prioritizing skills with the ability to multitask and work under the pressure of constant deadlines.
* Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy in all forms of communication.
* Ability to work independently while being in a high functioning team.
* Discretion with senior\-level confidential student information.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Associate or Bachelor’s degree.
* Two years of progressively independent and complex administrative support experience.
* Work experience in a health care setting or directly with physicians, and/or in higher education is strongly preferred.
* Advanced experience with Excel, Sharepoint, and Asana programs.

**Working Conditions**

* Occasional work beyond a standard 40\-hour work week may be required.
* Periodic evening and weekend work may be necessary to support events, presentations, meetings, and project deadlines.

The UW School of Medicine Spokane Medical Education Office is committed to delivering an exceptional medical education experience that prepares future physicians to serve diverse communities.
